transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-20 10:00 PDT | Duration: 45m
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Daniel Cho (Redwood SE), Lina Gomez (Redwood CSM); Samir Khan (Aurora Dir ML), Jenna Lee (Aurora Platform Eng), Marcus V. (Aurora SRE)

Summary: Weekly POC sync focused on Dedicated sizing and autoscaling policy. Reviewed recent pilot metrics, discussed burst behavior and warm pool strategy, clarified telemetry needed for final sizing, and agreed on next steps (tests + docs).

Topics: Dedicated autoscaling, min/max replica tuning, burst capacity, cold-start mitigation, KV cache/ prefix cache behavior, quantization/throughput tradeoffs, security gating for Dedicated deployment.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Samir Khan: Samir here, yep. Jenna and Marcus on my end too.
[00:10] Daniel Cho: Daniel from Redwood, hey all.
[00:12] Lina Gomez: Lina here.
[00:15] Maya Patel: Cool. Agenda — review last week's run, go over the Dedicated sizing suggestions we emailed, then plan a burst test. Any blockers?
[00:24] Samir Khan: Main thing is we saw latency spikes in the evening window when traffic hits ~850 rps. Average is around 400 rps during business hours. We want to avoid 95th > 500ms.
[00:35] Jenna Lee: Also we need to confirm network egress constraints and whether we can do VPC peering for Dedicated.
[00:42] Daniel Cho: Got it. Quick note — last week's run we left autoscale min at 2 and max at 12 for the Dedicated pool. We noticed cold starts on new replicas added under high burst, which added ~120-250ms on tail. Warm pool helps.
[00:56] Marcus V.: When you say "warm pool" do you mean reserved instances spun up ahead of anticipated traffic?
[01:02] Daniel Cho: Exactly. We can keep a few warm replicas idle (just initialized, model loaded) to absorb short bursts. That reduces cold-start latency but increases baseline cost.
[01:12] Samir Khan: What's the tradeoff — cost vs latency? Our SREs prefer slightly higher cost over tail latencies.
[01:18] Maya Patel: We'll show a couple of scenarios. For example, min_replicas=3 + warm_pool=2 can cut 99th by ~200ms for your load profile vs min_replicas=1. Cost bump is roughly 12-18% depending on model size/quantization.
[01:31] Jenna Lee: That aligns with what we care about. Also curious how batching impacts latency — we do a lot of short prompts.
[01:37] Daniel Cho: Batching increases throughput and amortizes kernel overhead, but for short prompts with strict latency you limit dynamic batching window. Our runtime supports micro-batching with low-delay thresholds; we can tune max_batch_wait_ms.
[01:49] Samir Khan: Can you remind us about KV cache behavior — do we persist prefix cache between requests? We saw some references to KV cache but not sure it's set up right.
[01:57] Daniel Cho: By default KV cache is per-session unless you enable longer-lived prefix caching. For chat workloads with repeated context patterns we recommend enabling prefix/KV caching at the model route. That reduces token compute on repeated parts. Note auto-eviction policies exist so you don't run OOM.
[02:12] Marcus V.: Is "K V cash" -- I mean KV cache -- affected by restart or scaling events?
[02:17] Daniel Cho: Good question. When a replica is terminated the in-memory KV cache is lost; warm pool helps because you keep replicas with cache warm. We're also exploring a shared cache layer but that wasn't in this pilot.
[02:29] Maya Patel: On the pilot metrics you shared — we parsed a 72h sample. We see two notable peaks and one sustained evening plateau. I'll pull up the graph.
[02:36] [screen share / brief pause]
[02:48] Maya Patel: So this is the 24h histogram — your 95th during peak is ~620ms, 99th is ~1.1s. Under the current Dedicated config min=2/max=12. Most of the 99th is from scale-ups and cold-starts.
[03:02] Samir Khan: If we bump min to 4 does that flatten tail?
[03:07] Daniel Cho: Yes, increasing min reduces the need to scale during the short bursts, but it also increases cost. Another option is aggressive warm_pool + faster node provisioning for burst replicas. We can also set scale-down cooldowns so replicas don't spin down quickly.
[03:20] Jenna Lee: How fast can we provision new replicas in Dedicated? We're looking at sub-60s ideally.
[03:26] Daniel Cho: Typical provision times vary by model size and infra — for the medium LLM we saw ~35-70s; larger models can be longer. Warm pool reduces user-visible time to <10-20ms for routing but initial replica actually takes that 35-70s.
[03:40] Samir Khan: Hmm — 35-70s is a lot if we get sudden spikes. Will warm pool cover those?
[03:45] Daniel Cho: If warm_pool size covers the burst magnitude then yes. Otherwise you can combine warm_pool with burst_quota that temporarily allows more requests through degraded model variants (smaller quantized model) until replicas are ready.
[03:58] Marcus V.: That degraded model fallback — is that automatic? How do you ensure quality?
[04:04] Maya Patel: It's policy-driven. You define compatible model variants and thresholds. If latency SLOs are at risk, router can route a percentage to a cheaper variant with automatic rollback if quality metrics decline. We can hook your eval prompts to automate that signal.
[04:20] Samir Khan: We care about data isolation. If we use Dedicated, does data ever leave our VPC?
[04:26] Daniel Cho: For Dedicated in your tenant we keep data isolated. For Private (VPC/on-prem) you can have an entirely customer-managed network. For the pilot if you require VPC peering we can set that up; we'll need network configs from Jenna.
[04:38] Jenna Lee: I'll confirm firewall rules and whether peering is allowed.
[04:42] Maya Patel: Back to sizing — we proposed two scenarios in the doc: conservative (min=3, max=12, warm_pool=2) and aggressive (min=5, max=20, warm_pool=4) with cost and latency estimates. Which looks better?
[04:55] Samir Khan: Start conservative, but with ability to run short bursts. If the 95th is still >500ms, we can move to aggressive.
[05:01] Daniel Cho: Sounds good. For the burst test we'll simulate 1.5x and 2x peak for 10 minutes and observe scale-up behavior and 99th latency. We'll also confirm that autoscaler cooldowns don't cause flapping.
[05:13] Marcus V.: About quantization — we looked at int8 and int4 notes. Does quantization affect scale times?
[05:19] Daniel Cho: Slightly. Smaller quantized models have faster load time and lower memory footprint, so provisioning can be faster. But int4 may change quality. We'll include a quick A/B quality check as part of the test.
[05:32] Samir Khan: Can you also include token-level cost estimates per 1M tokens for each scenario?
[05:38] Maya Patel: Yes I'll include a cost model sheet. That will show per-token compute cost, plus reserved replica cost for warm pools.
[05:44] Jenna Lee: One more thing — audit logs and KMS. We need confirmation that all requests and model outputs are logged and accessible for audits, and that keys are customer-managed.
[05:55] Lina Gomez: We have integrations with KMS and can enable customer-managed keys for Private/Dedicated deployments. Audit logs are available and we can export them to your logging infra. We'll follow up with the SOC2 pack.
[06:07] Samir Khan: Great.
[06:10] [short cross-talk]
[06:18] Daniel Cho: Quick clarifying question — for the burst test do you want a synthetic rush pattern (spike then decay) or a sustained plateau?
[06:25] Samir Khan: Synthetic spike first, then a sustained plateau of 1.2x for 15 minutes. That will show both scale-up behavior and steady-state.
[06:33] Daniel Cho: Perfect. We'll schedule the burst test Wednesday morning — I can run it in our staging Dedicated environment but with same model and config.
[06:41] Maya Patel: Action: Daniel to run test and upload full logs. Samir to share prod histograms. Jenna to confirm networking. I'll send updated sizing doc.
[06:50] Samir Khan: Sounds good. Any other risks?
[06:53] Marcus V.: We should monitor GPU memory OOMs with KV cache and large batch combos.
[06:58] Daniel Cho: We'll add telemetry for GPU memory and per-replica CPU. Also enable early OOM alerts.
[07:07] Maya Patel: Ok final recap — next steps and owners are in the action items. We'll reconvene next Tuesday at the same time after the burst test and updated docs.
[07:18] Jenna Lee: Thanks everyone.
[07:20] Samir Khan: Thank you.
[07:22] Daniel Cho: Thanks.

End of transcript.
